GRAMMAR -ing clauses
We can add clauses that begin with a verb in the
-ing form to a sentence. It explains what someone /
something is, or was, doing at a particular time.
I suddenly noticed a group of crows looking quite
excited.
(= I suddenly noticed a group of crows. They were
looking quite excited).
I suddenly saw this huge snake lying across the road.
(= I suddenly saw this huge snake. It was lying across
the road.)

CONVERSATION PRACTICE
• A Think of any strange or unusual animals you
have seen - or any animals you have seen doing
something strange. Think about where they were
and what they were doing when you saw them.
Think about how you felt and what happened. Then
work in groups. Tell some other students about your
experiences. When one person finishes their story,
another should try to tell a similar story. Use these
expressions to connect the stories:
It reminds me of something I once saw...
It actually reminds me of something that happened
to me..
